methodological_rigor.justification: The study applies ReSisTrace lineage tracing in FLT3-ITD MOLM-13 cells with thoughtful controls: DMSO pre-fitness signature to separate resistance-specific from growth-related transcriptional states, dual cell-line validation (MOLM-13, MV4-11), two diagnostic-stage primary AML patient samples, CRISPR-Cas9 GSPT1 knockout with dual gRNAs to corroborate drug findings, and an FLT3-ITD PDX mouse model with n=8/group and four groups (vehicle, quizartinib, CC-90009, combination). Multiple synergy scoring methods (HSA, Bliss, Loewe, ZIP) are applied for concordance. Limitations include single cell-line ReSisTrace (MOLM-13 only), only two patient samples (limiting generalizability), heterozygous FLT3-ITD in MOLM-13 (acknowledged as potential confounder), and thymidine synchronization potentially introducing noise (acknowledged). Statistics use two-tailed t-tests with Holm multiplicity correction, bootstrap significance for synergy, pairwise log-rank with Holm for survival, and FDR-adjusted thresholds for DEGs - generally strong.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical study combining cell lines, primary patient samples, and PDX models (LoE 5). Clinical relevance is high: the identified drugs have existing clinical development pipelines (CC-90009 clinical experience discussed including termination of NCT02848001/NCT04336982 and follow-on BMS-986497 NCT06419634; vistusertib, linsitinib, meisoindigo phase I/III safety data cited). The proposed combinations directly target the clinically important problem of FLT3 inhibitor resistance in AML and are actionable for rational trial design.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies to the PDX animal study; reporting includes strain RRID, regulatory approvals (Norwegian Animal Research Authority, AAALAC), randomization by weight and bioluminescence, vehicle controls, dosing details, and pre-specified outcome measures (tumor burden, survival). Cell line RRIDs, mycoplasma testing, antibody catalog with RRIDs, and detailed CRISPR guide sequences are provided. Biobank ethics approvals (FHRB, Helsinki UCH) are stated for patient samples. Data availability for scRNA-seq data is not explicitly addressed in the visible text, though Supplementary Tables are referenced (gene lists) - GEO/SRA deposition status is unclear; code for ReSisTrace analysis references prior Dai 2024 publication. ARRIVE gaps: no sample size justification, blinding not explicit for imaging analysis.

novelty_literature.justification: The work applies a lineage-tracing method (ReSisTrace, authors' prior Dai 2024 Nat Commun) for the first time to hematological cancers and FLT3 inhibitor resistance. The connectivity-map-based strategy to predict pre-sensitizing drugs via reversal of pre-resistance signatures is methodologically novel in this context, and the identification of GSPT1 as a pre-resistance gene with CC-90009 synergy adds concrete therapeutic value. Not a first-in-class concept (connectivity map repurposing and DTP state biology are established), but the integration of lineage tracing + L1000 drug prediction + multimodal validation in primary AML and PDX is a meaningful extension that fills a documented gap.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical structure from ReSisTrace workflow through signature discovery, drug prediction, in vitro and patient sample validation, to in vivo confirmation. Figures are described with appropriate quantitative context, and the discussion candidly addresses limitations (heterozygous FLT3-ITD, dilution of pre-sensitive signal, L1000 solid-tumor-biased database). Minor typographic issues (e.g., 'GSPT1 was depletion was incomplete', 'ClinicalTrilas.gov') but overall the scientific narrative is coherent and precise.

key_strengths: Creative application of ReSisTrace lineage tracing to FLT3-ITD AML with rigorous DMSO control to separate pre-fitness from pre-resistance transcriptional states
Concordant synergy across four scoring methods (HSA, Bliss, Loewe, ZIP) and validation in two independent FLT3-ITD cell lines plus two primary patient samples
Mechanistic confirmation via CRISPR-Cas9 GSPT1 knockout and western blot degradation evidence
In vivo PDX combination efficacy with appropriate randomization and pairwise log-rank with Holm correction
Systematic L1000-based repurposing identifying vistusertib, linsitinib, meisoindigo - all with existing clinical safety profiles cited
key_concerns: ReSisTrace performed in only one cell line (MOLM-13); generalizability depends on downstream validation in MV4-11 and primary samples only
Only two primary patient samples limit generalizability across AML genetic/clinical diversity
PDX study uses a single patient model (AML-PDX1); response heterogeneity across patient backgrounds not assessed in vivo
GSPT1 knockout efficiency modest (65% protein reduction) with transient fitness effects complicating interpretation
Data availability for scRNA-seq deposition not explicitly stated; code availability for ReSisTrace processing not clearly documented in this manuscript
Discussion of CC-90009's terminated clinical trials (NCT02848001, NCT04336982) flags a translational liability warranting stronger contextualization
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sophisticated preclinical study with strong in vitro and in vivo validation of lineage-tracing-derived combination strategies warrants Tier 2 (Clinical Cancer Research, Cancer Research, Leukemia). It is not a first-in-class methodologic invention and has generalizability limits from single-cell-line tracing and few patient samples; minor revisions to data/code availability and clinical trial context would strengthen.
